findings.reason: Proof steps 1.2 and 2.1 use pullback/exterior-derivative commutation for Phi_X, which is C2 from X being C3, while the cited theorems require smooth maps. State Phi_X's C2 regularity and provide the finite-regularity coordinate proof or an exact C2 supplier.

Clause 3 quantifies over overlapping charts, but proof 4.1 only constructs transitions where the maps are local diffeomorphisms. State that transition hypothesis (including the relevant dimensions). The proof's final lambda-to-lambda+dF claim also infers exactness from closedness; retain only the closed-one-form conclusion.

The definition allows maps between phase domains of different dimensions, including the lower-dimensional generalized-coordinate immersions, but the cited matrix test assumes equal dimensions. Its local-diffeomorphism, determinant, and field-transport consequences do not hold for general symplectic embeddings. Distinguish dimension-aware pullback-preserving embeddings from equal-dimensional canonical transformations, and limit those consequences accordingly.

The statement permits any canonical map, but the iff proof in steps 1.1 and 3.1 uses an inverse derivative. Require an equal-dimensional local diffeomorphism/canonical transformation and limit the chart instances to genuine transitions.

The volume form has degree 6N, so its pullback is not the phase-volume form on a lower-dimensional symplectic embedding. Qualify the 'every canonical map' statement and chart-measure comparison to equal-dimensional transformations and genuine chart transitions; state the phase-volume unit as action to the power 3N.

The bracket of C2 functions is only guaranteed C1, so the C2 class is not a Poisson algebra. The cited finite-regularity definition explicitly makes no C2-closure claim. Preserve the listed lower-regularity identities and state the Poisson-algebra conclusion for a closed class such as C-infinity.
The statement declares f:U->R on a phase-space open set but then uses f(t,z(t)) and partial_t f. Define f on an open time-phase neighborhood of the solution graph, with its C1 regularity there.

Proof step 3.1 applies the cited Jacobi result to f, g, and H, although H is only assumed C2 and the supplier states Jacobi for three C3 functions. Add the mixed-regularity coordinate proof for f,g C3 and H C2 using the C1 bracket extension, or state the stronger H regularity.

Phi_t is only C1, so compositions of C2 test functions are generally C1. Identify the exact finite-regularity definition that extends the coordinate bracket to C1 functions in Facts and use it in the bracket-preservation statement and proof.

With H only C1, sigma has continuous coefficients, not a smooth differential form as cited. Define sigma as the needed continuous coordinate 2-form and justify its displayed coordinate derivative, or strengthen the regularity hypothesis.

The cited inverse-function theorem supplies a C1 inverse, while the generating-function definitions and cited propositions use a C2 inverse. Add the derivative-formula argument that a C2 map's local inverse is C2. Step 2.1 also uses smooth pullback/d commutation for C2 parameter maps; differentiate the one-form identity directly at its stated regularity. State that S has action dimension and S_t energy dimension.

The derivative is called block diagonal in interleaved (x1,p1,x2,p2,x3,p3) order, while the declared Cartesian order is grouped (x,p). Specify the permutation and corresponding J, or verify the grouped block matrix. Declare [k]=mass/time^2, [omega_0]=1/time, and the action^3 units of the six-dimensional phase volume.
State that the generating function S_t has action dimension, consistent with the declared momentum, position, and time units.
State the action dimension of S(q,P) and the conjugate units of the generalized and Cartesian momentum slots used in P dot X(q).

Claim 4 invokes the local and finite-time error suppliers without their hypotheses: the compact convex tube and derivative bounds, small-step condition, and retention of exact and numerical trajectories in the compact set. Carry these conditions into the claim. Declare h as a time step and k's stiffness units; the Euclidean error norm mixes position and momentum coordinates, so specify its normalization or coordinate-dependent numerical meaning.

The determinant-test paragraph says the matrix criterion applies to any C1 map of the presentation. Qualify it to equal-dimensional phase domains; lower-dimensional maps require the dimension-aware pullback condition.
